newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish bonds ended down but above day-lows on Thursday as dealers grew nervous that worries over European economic and monetary union could provoke a sell-off.
"We saw a high trading volume at the end. To me that means the market is positioning for a big move, which is very likely to be downward," said Emilio Sainz at Natwest in Madrid.
He added that U.S. first-quarter GDP data on Friday and the squaring of books ahead of the second round of the French election on Sunday could also prompt a correction.
Other dealers agreed with the diagnosis, but said that positive Spanish fundamentals could provide support.
But next month's regular Treasury refunding could also weigh on the market, Sainz said.
On the cash market the 10-year spread over Bunds finished almost unchanged at around 74 basis points from 75 basis points at the close on Wednesday. German markets were closed for a public holiday.
